transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-11 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes | Attendees: Alice Johnson (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Liu (Redwood SE), Tom Reynolds (MidState Head of Data), Meera Singh (CISO), Luis Gomez (Cloud Architect), Erin Park (Product).

00:00 - Alice Johnson: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick intro — i'm alice, i'm the AE on this account, ravi and maya from our SE team will cover the technical bits. could we do quick intros on the bank side?
00:12 - Tom Reynolds: yeah tom here, head of data. we're evaluating options for hosting LLMs for customer-facing summaries and a fraud-detection assistant. primary concerns are data residency, retention, and regulatory logging.
00:25 - Meera Singh: meera, ciso. we need to understand if we can use hosted redwood or if we need dedicated/private. HIPAA isn't primary but we do have financial regs and some PII. also GDPR, obviously.
00:38 - Luis Gomez: luis - cloud architect. current infra is aws (eu-west-1 + us-east-1), we have strict egress rules and only allow managed outbound to certain services.
00:47 - Alice Johnson: got it. high level — redwood offers hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (vpc/on-prem). typical pattern for banks is start with dedicated or private depending on data residency and audit needs. we'll talk through tradeoffs.
01:05 - Erin Park: timeline wise we have exec review mid-july, pilot decision by end of june would be ideal.
01:12 - Alice Johnson: perfect, that aligns. ravi, maybe you can walk through deployments and residency options?
01:18 - Ravi Patel: sure. so from a deployments perspective we have three options. hosted api is our managed cloud product — it's fast to get started but data may be processed in multi-tenant infra; we provide contractual controls and data handling guarantees. dedicated is reserved GPU pools just for you, isolated at the tenant level and can be region pinned. private gives you a private control plane and can be deployed in your VPC or on-prem where all inference happens in your network.
01:40 - Meera Singh: for us, the key questions are 1) where do logs go, 2) can we prevent any customer PII from being retained, 3) what evidence can you provide for audits.
01:51 - Ravi Patel: great questions. for logs: hosted by default stores minimal metadata needed for monitoring and billing. we offer configurable logging, and for dedicated/private we can disable or route logs to your s3/elk with customer-managed encryption keys. retention is configurable; by default hosted keeps 90 days, but we can negotiate retention for enterprise contracts.
02:12 - Tom Reynolds: when you say logs routed to our s3, does that mean we get the raw transcripts and model outputs? that would be risky.
02:20 - Maya Liu: typically we separate telemetry from content. raw transcripts/model outputs are optional and in dedicated/private they're under your control. in hosted we avoid storing full outputs unless you opt in; we store cost/latency metrics. but for your use-case, most banks request private or dedicated with logging pushed to customer's storage to meet policy.
02:39 - Meera Singh: okay and encryption? we need KMS/HSM support and customer-managed keys for any logs or artifacts that leave our VPC.
02:47 - Ravi Patel: yes we integrate with customer KMS for dedicated/private. for hosted we have managed keys but can offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options for enterprise arrangements. HSM-level attestations can be discussed; we can share our key management docs and how we handle envelope encryption.
03:03 - Luis Gomez: network - we can't have broad egress. Would dedicated allow no internet egress except to redwood control plane, or do you need other endpoints?
03:12 - Ravi Patel: in private / vpc we can operate with minimal egress — control plane endpoints for orchestration, telemetry pushed to your endpoints, and model weights can be staged in your region. for dedicated, there's a managed plane but we can restrict endpoints and whitelist IP ranges. we'll need to map exact endpoints for firewall rules.
03:28 - Tom Reynolds: GDPR — data residency: can you guarantee processing stays in eu-west-1 for EU customers?
03:35 - Maya Liu: yes, you can pin model serving to a region. for hosted we have regional clusters; for strict residency we recommend private deployment in your VPC or dedicated region pinned pools. note that some emergency failover could route to other regions unless you enforce stricter routing rules. we can put contractual SLOs and routing constraints.
03:57 - Meera Singh: auditability — SOC2, ISO, penetration tests? we will need artifacts for our third-party risk team.
04:06 - Alice Johnson: we are SOC2 Type II and have ISO27001 summary, and we do regular pentests. i'll share the certification pack after this call.
04:13 - Meera Singh: do you have a redact / pii detection capability pre-ingest? we may want client-side redaction before sending anything off prem.
04:21 - Ravi Patel: we have SDKs that allow client-side filtering and can run lightweight PII detectors in your app. for higher-assurance workflows with PII, we recommend private deployment so that content never leaves your network.
04:36 - Luis Gomez: can you speak to model artifacts? we need to know where model weights live and whether any telemetry is sent back to redwood for model improvement.
04:44 - Maya Liu: model weights can be stored in your cloud for private deployments; for dedicated we can host them in a customer-dedicated bucket in the region. telemetry for product improvement is opt-in; by default we do not use customer data to train models unless you opt in. we can also disable debug dumps.
04:59 - Tom Reynolds: ok good. performance — our latency SLO is sub-200ms p50 for short prompts, and less than 2s p90 for longer interactions. can you meet that from eu-west-1?
05:10 - Ravi Patel: yes for dedicated pools we routinely see that latency. for private, depends on your infra; we provide kernel selection and batching configs to tune performance. we can run benchmarks in your staging env as part of the pilot.
05:25 - Meera Singh: compliance question — e-discovery and legal holds. if regulator asks for transcripts, how do we provide them and what is redwood's role?
05:34 - Alice Johnson: for dedicated/private, logs and outputs live in your storage so you control discovery. for hosted there are contractual mechanisms; we can support data export requests. we'll include specifics in the legal pack.
05:46 - Erin Park: cost — can you outline the major cost drivers between hosted, dedicated, and private?
05:53 - Maya Liu: hosted is pay-as-you-go per token and embeddings; cheapest to start but less isolation. dedicated is monthly committed capacity — you pay for reserved GPUs but get consistent throughput and lower per-token cost. private includes additional infra and support costs. we'll provide a sample TCO for your anticipated throughput.
06:10 - Tom Reynolds: what's the onboarding time for private vs dedicated?
06:15 - Ravi Patel: dedicated can be provisioned in a few weeks depending on capacity and contract. private/vpc takes longer — typically 6-8 weeks for a first deployment including networking, KMS integration, and compliance checks.
06:27 - Meera Singh: do you support SSO/SAML and RBAC? we need centralized access control and audit trails.
06:33 - Maya Liu: yes. we support SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, and granular RBAC. audit logs are available and can be forwarded to your SIEM.
06:45 - Luis Gomez: any limitations on model quantization or custom models in private?
06:50 - Ravi Patel: you can bring custom models; our runtime supports common formats and quantized weights. some model ops may require additional compat testing, but generally we can onboard models with a short validation.
07:04 - Tom Reynolds: regarding retention — you said hosted keeps 90 days by default. what's the contractual lowest you support?
07:11 - Alice Johnson: we can negotiate retention windows down to 0 days for outputs for enterprise contracts on dedicated/private — meaning you opt-out of storing outputs entirely. telemetry still exists for billing but can be minimized and scrubbed. we'll include specifics in the security pack.
07:28 - Meera Singh: can you provide a diagram of how data flows in each deployment? we need that for our third-party risk assessment.
07:36 - Ravi Patel: yes, i'll prepare diagrams for hosted, dedicated and private that show where logs, model weights, and telemetry flow.
07:44 - Erin Park: for the pilot, we want a staging region in eu-west-1 and data residency guarantees for EU customers. can you run a 2-week benchmark?
07:52 - Alice Johnson: yes, we can set up a pilot with a staging account. typical pilot includes traffic replay, latency/cost baseline, and a security questionnaire response.
08:02 - Luis Gomez: firewall rules — we need a sparse list of endpoints and IP ranges, can you provide that?
08:08 - Maya Liu: we'll share a minimal whitelist and CPU/GPU endpoints.
08:14 - Meera Singh: one more — legal/contract: do you accept data processing addendum (DPA) with EU standard contractual clauses?
08:20 - Alice Johnson: yes, we include DPAs and can support SCCs where needed for EU data flows.
08:26 - Tom Reynolds: any customers in finance you can reference?
08:29 - Alice Johnson: we have multiple regional banks and fintechs; we'll share references in the follow up.
08:36 - Speaker 1: [unintelligible]
08:40 - Ravi Patel: quick clarifying Q on logging: you mentioned internal policy prohibits long-term retention of PII. do you want us to redact at the SDK side or avoid storing outputs entirely?
08:50 - Meera Singh: prefer redact pre-ingest but also have the option to never store outputs. we need both options documented.
08:58 - Alice Johnson: noted. action items are: i'll send SOC2/ISO and DPA; ravi will prepare infra diagrams and latency estimates; we'll propose pilot steps and pricing.
09:10 - Erin Park: can you include a checklist for our compliance team? they want explicit items: encryption details, KMS flow, audit log retention, pentest dates, vendor risk contact.
09:22 - Maya Liu: yes we'll deliver a compliance checklist tailored for financial services.
09:27 - Tom Reynolds: ok next steps for us — internal alignment, compile a short list of test prompts (we have some fraud scenarios), and get net new firewall rules ready.
09:37 - Alice Johnson: thanks everyone. we'll aim to follow up with docs and schedule the tech deep dive for 2025-06-18.
09:45 - Meera Singh: thanks.
09:47 - Luis Gomez: thanks all.
09:50 - Alice Johnson: end meeting.

Meeting summary: MidState Bank is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing summaries and fraud-assist. Primary concerns are GDPR data residency, PII retention and redaction, KMS/HSM integration, audit evidence (SOC2/ISO/pentest), and network egress restrictions. Preferred pilot in eu-west-1, target exec decision mid-july.

Action items (recap): 
- Alice Johnson: Share SOC2/ISO pack, DPA, and SCCs.
- Ravi Patel: Prepare deployment diagrams and baseline latency & cost estimates for Dedicated and Private.
- Luis Gomez (customer): Confirm network egress constraints and allowed endpoints.

References shared: Security docs (link placeholder), regional deployment checklist (link placeholder), pilot proposal spreadsheet (link placeholder).
